title: 1. The Hook
text: Imagine you have a friend who lives very, very far away. It would take you days to walk to their house! Your legs would get so tired. How can you visit them quickly without walking?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking
text: Why do you think birds can travel so fast while we walk slowly? What if we had something that could move faster than our legs?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Moving Things
content.description: Just like a bird uses wings to fly and a fish uses fins to swim, we use different machines with wheels to move faster. Watch how wheels help a cart move quickly!

title: 4. Reveal: Means of Transport
text: The vehicles we use to travel from one place to another are called Means of Transport. We use different vehicles to travel on land, on water, and in the air.

content.meaning: Ways to move people or goods from one place to another.
A machine, usually with wheels and an engine, used for transporting people or goods.

question: Which of these helps us travel fast on land?
If you want to cross a river, what vehicle will you use?

title: 6. Reflection
text: Think about how you came to school today. Did you walk? Did you come by bus, auto, or bicycle? Explain to your teacher why you chose that vehicle.

title: 7. Connection
text: Long ago, in ancient India, people used animals like horses, elephants, and bullock carts to travel. Today, we use engines to make our vehicles run. All these help us explore our big, beautiful world!

content.title: 8. Mastery: My Transport Book
content.description: Look outside your window. Count how many different types of vehicles you can see. Draw your favorite vehicle and color it!

content.title: Oops! Did you know?
content.text: A train is a land transport, but it cannot run on normal roads. It needs special iron tracks called rails!

content.title: For the Teacher
content.text: Use toy cars, a paper boat, and a paper plane in the classroom to physically demonstrate the three modes of transport: Land, Water, and Air.
